articles.title: The Australian Open’s animated livestreams make players look like Wii Sports characters
articles.summary: The Australian Open is airing animated versions of its games alongside real matches, making players look like Wii-Sports-style characters.
articles.body: The Australian Open might look a little different this year if you’re livestreaming it on YouTube. That’s because the tournament has put an animated overlay on some of its matches to avoid broadcast licensing conflicts, making players look an awful lot like Wii Sports characters, as reported earlier by The Guardian. The animated players follow all the same movements as their real-life counterparts as they travel across a cartoon-ish court, while the “whap” of the ball, chatter from the crowd, and commentary all remain authentic. But the animations aren’t perfect, as the players’ sneakers seem to clip into the court at some points, while Naomi Osaka’s animated tank top looked like it was ripped during her match against Caroline Garcia. [Image: Naomi Osaka’s tank top didn’t look quite right. With the animated livestreams, the Australian Open can air its games on YouTube without conflicting with the broadcasting agreements it sold to networks and streaming services around the world, according to The Guardian. The technology, which the Australian Open first introduced last year, uses 12 cameras to “process the silhouette of the human in real time, and stitch that together across 29 points in the skeleton,” Machar Reid, the director of innovation at Tennis Australia, the organization behind the tournament, told The Guardian. “It’s not as seamless as it could be — we don’t have fingers — but in time you can begin to imagine a world where that comes.” [Media: Based on the information from the sensors, the Australian Open’s systems can then create an animated version of the live events with a two-minute delay. We’ve seen other broadcasters and sports leagues experiment with creating alternate telecasts of games as well. During the Super Bowl LVIII, CBS Sports partnered with Nickelodeon to add Spongebob Squarepants and slime animations to the big game, while the NFL aired an animated football game featuring The Simpsons last year.

articles.title: Star Wars’ original theatrical cut returns to theaters in 2027
articles.summary: Disney is bringing a “newly restored version” of the original, 1977 theatrical cut of Star Wars back to theaters on February 19th, 2027.
articles.body: Disney is bringing a “newly restored version” of the original, 1977 theatrical cut of Star Wars back to theaters on February 19th, 2027. It will only be available in theaters for “a limited time,” Disney says, and it’s being released as part of “Lucasfilm’s yearlong 50th anniversary celebration” for the franchise. Tickets aren’t on sale yet, but Disney says it will share details on when and where to buy tickets on StarWars.com. Disney initially revealed earlier this year that it would be bringing Star Wars back to theaters. Star Wars creator George Lucas has famously tinkered with what’s now called A New Hope, but a few lucky fans have already been able to recently see the first theatrical cut; The British Film Institute showed an original, 35mm release print of the movie in June at an event that featured an introduction from Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy, who confirmed that it was “in fact, the first print.” Ahead of the re-release of the first Star Wars, Disney is bringing The Mandalorian and Grogu to theaters on May 22nd, 2026. Another film, Star Wars: Starfighter, starring Ryan Gosling, is coming to theaters on May 28th, 2027.

articles.title: Jason Segel Marries Kayla Radomski
articles.summary: The 'Shrinking' star and 'So You Think You Can Dance' alum have tied the knot after more than two years together.
articles.body:
The Shrinking star and How I Met Your Mother alum and his longtime girlfriend, So You Think You Can Dance alum Kayla Radomski, have tied the knot.

The pair were married Saturday at the Huntington Library Botanical Gardens in Pasadena, according to an Instagram Stories post from a friend, seen by People .

Radomski, who announced her engagement to Segel on Instagram in June 2025, shared numerous posts to her Instagram stories from friends and family celebrating her and Segel's nuptials.

Segel and Radomski have made numerous public appearances together over the past two years, with Radomski accompanying him to several awards shows, where he's been nominated for his lead role in Shrinking , the Apple TV comedy co-starring Harrison Ford.

After Shrinking aired its third season earlier this year, it was renewed for season four, but creator Bill Lawrence said there will be a time jump and a "completely different story" in the upcoming season.

Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter at a PaleyFest LA event after the fourth-season renewal was announced, Segel said he hoped for a happier arc for his character, who ended season three pursuing a romance with Sofi, played by his How I Met Your Mother co-star Cobie Smulders.

"Maybe it's time for Jimmy to try to have some fun," Segel said of his character. "We've seen Jimmy going through it, but it's been with an emotional twisted ankle. We need to see him run a little bit and break out."

Onscreen, Segel's character also officiated the third-season-premiere wedding between Ford's Paul and Wendie Malick's Julie.

In addition to Shrinking and How I Met Your Mother , Segel's credits include Freaks and Geeks; I Love You, Man; Forgetting Sarah Marshall ; the 2011 Muppets movie, which he also wrote and executive produced; Despicable Me; Bad Teacher; Sex Tape; The Five-Year Engagement ; The End of the Tour , in which he played David Foster Wallace; Winning Time; Over My Dead Body ; and Dispatches From Elsewhere .

In addition to roles as a dancer in movies like Michael, Once Upon a Time in Hollywood and The Greatest Showman , Radomski also guest-starred in two episodes of the second and final season of Palm Royale and appeared alongside Segel in Over My Dead Body and Winning Time .

A rep for Segel has not yet responded to The Hollywood Reporter 's request for comment.

articles.title: Festival de teatro infantil reúne seis espetáculos e companhias de todo país em Sorocaba; saiba como assistir | G1
articles.standfirst: FESTINCABA será realizado de 21 a 23 de outubro, no Céu das Artes Laranjeiras, com apresentações voltadas exclusivamente a estudantes de escolas públicas.
articles.summary: FESTINCABA será realizado de 21 a 23 de outubro, no Céu das Artes Laranjeiras, com apresentações voltadas exclusivamente a estudantes de escolas públicas.
articles.body:
Festival de teatro infantil reúne seis espetáculos e companhias de todo país em Sorocaba — Foto: Divulgação

O Festival de Teatro Infantil de Sorocaba (Festincaba) realiza sua terceira edição entre esta quart (21) e sexta-feira (23), no Céu das Artes Laranjeiras, na zona norte da cidade. A programação gratuita reúne seis espetáculos de companhias de São Paulo, Goiás e Rio de Janeiro, com sessões às 10h30 e às 14h.

Nesta edição, o festival é voltado exclusivamente a estudantes de escolas públicas. A curadoria selecionou as apresentações entre 108 inscrições recebidas de diferentes regiões do país. Na edição anterior, foram 99 propostas.

Segundo a organização, o evento busca ampliar o acesso ao teatro infantil em regiões com menor oferta de atividades culturais. Esta é a primeira vez que o festival ocupa um equipamento cultural da periferia de Sorocaba.

“Receber essa quantidade de inscrições em tão pouco tempo surpreende e, ao mesmo tempo, confirma que o Festincaba conquistou seu espaço no calendário do teatro infantil brasileiro”, afirma Priscila Maldonado, produtora e proponente do festival.

10h30: Charanga da Tramp, da Cia. Tramp de Palhaços, de Jundiaí (SP).

14h: Cem Histórias Sem Palavras, da Cia. Dois que Contam, de Campinas (SP).

10h30: Circus a Nova Tournée, da Cia. Circo de Bonecos, de Salto (SP).

14h: Inventando Moda, da Cia. Boca do Lixo, de Anápolis (GO).

10h30: Os Monstros que os Medos Criam, da Cia. Teatral Passarinhada, de São Paulo (SP).

14h: As Aventuras de Quitapena, da Lamparina Produções Culturais, do Rio de Janeiro (RJ).

Estudantes também participam de oficinas

Festival de teatro infantil reúne seis espetáculos e companhias de todo país em Sorocaba; — Foto: Divulgação

Além das apresentações, os estudantes participarão de três workshops com atividades de técnicas circenses básicas, jogos teatrais e mágicas.

Entre as instituições com presença confirmada estão as escolas estaduais Monteiro Lobato, Antônio Cordeiro e Roque Conceição Martins; as escolas municipais Professora Odilla Caldini Crespo e Professor Ney Oliveira Fogaça, conhecida como Quintal; além da Casa do Menor de Sorocaba, da Associação Sorocabana de Atividades para Deficientes Visuais (ASAC) e da Integra Surdos Sorocaba.

Todas as sessões terão acessibilidade em Língua Brasileira de Sinais (Libras), segundo a organização. Também está prevista uma sessão especial com audiodescrição.

“Para nós, o maior resultado do Festincaba acontece no momento em que as crianças entram no teatro e a plateia se enche de risadas, curiosidade e emoção. Isso mostra o quanto o investimento em cultura pode transformar a rotina de cada comunidade”, afirma Rodrigo Cintra, gestor cultural do projeto.

O Festincaba é realizado pela Pri Produção Artística, com apoio do Ponto de Cultura Barracão da Vó. O projeto foi contemplado pelo edital PNAB nº 01/2026, na categoria Festivais, da Secretaria da Cultura de Sorocaba, com recursos da Política Nacional Aldir Blanc, do Ministério da Cultura.

articles.title: Amy Winehouse bought her first Camden flat in 2003 with money from her debut album Frank; 23 years later, the two-bedroom home has returned to the market for £650,000
articles.summary: Amy Winehouse’s first home in Camden has gone on sale for £650,000, more than 23 years after the singer bought the two-bedroom maisonette as her music
articles.body: Amy Winehouse’s first home in Camden has gone on sale for £650,000, more than 23 years after the singer bought the two-bedroom maisonette as her music career was beginning. The property, in Jeffrey’s Place, was reportedly purchased in 2003 using an advance for her debut album, Frank. According to The Sun, Winehouse lived there for around five years, including during the period when her second album, Back to Black, was released in October 2006 and brought her international recognition. She died in July 2011, aged 27, and Camden has remained closely associated with her music and legacy. The listing offers a glimpse into an early chapter of the singer’s life in the north London neighbourhood that became closely linked with her public image.Amy Winehouse’s first Camden flat listed for £650,000The two-bedroom maisonette in Jeffrey’s Place was reportedly the first home Winehouse bought for herself. She purchased it in 2003, the year Frank was released, and is believed to have used an advance for the album to fund the purchase, according to The Sun. The asking price is £650,000. The property’s association with Winehouse gives it a history beyond its position in the London housing market, although the asking price should not be confused with a confirmed sale price or an independent valuation.Winehouse reportedly lived at the flat for around five years, during a period when she was developing her sound and building her career. Frank blended jazz and soul influences with personal songwriting and earned a nomination for the Mercury Prize in 2004. Her second album, Back to Black, released in October 2006, brought her much wider international recognition. The price Winehouse paid for the property in 2003 has not been established in the available reporting. It is therefore not possible to calculate how much its value may have increased over the intervening years.How Camden became central to Amy Winehouse’s legacyCamden remained closely connected to Winehouse as her career developed. After Frank, the success of Back to Black made her one of Britain’s most prominent singers. She won five Grammy Awards in 2008 and received widespread recognition for her music and songwriting. Winehouse later lived at a property in Camden Square. She died on July 23, 2011, aged 27, from alcohol poisoning. Her death brought renewed attention to the north London neighbourhood associated with her music, public appearances and personal life. Her final home, a house overlooking Camden Square, was initially marketed for £2.7 million after her death. The property was later offered at auction with a guide price of £1.8 million and sold on December 3, 2012, for £1.98 million. Her family had said that none of them felt it was appropriate to live there, while her father, Mitch Winehouse, cited the cost of security and maintaining the house as reasons for selling it.A bronze statue of Winehouse was unveiled at Stables Market in Camden in 2014, creating another landmark for fans visiting the area. The Amy Winehouse Foundation, established after her death, works to support young people and people affected by addiction. The Jeffrey’s Place flat remained part of Winehouse’s life in Camden as her career developed, spanning the period around the release of both Frank and Back to Black. Its £650,000 listing has brought renewed attention to the home she reportedly bought with her debut album advance and to the north London neighbourhood that remained central to her life and legacy.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.summary: Tamil comedian and actor Vadivelu, popularly known as Vaigai Puyal, has added a new property to his life away from the big screen.
articles.body: Tamil comedian and actor Vadivelu, popularly known as Vaigai Puyal, has added a new property to his life away from the big screen. The actor’s new house has drawn attention for its traditional design and modern facilities. Starting from the verandah reminiscent of old-style Tamil houses right up to the solar panel and surveillance camera, the premises offer an amalgamation of village-style and modern facilities. There is also a garden with fruit trees, a parking place, and a separate office room for the actor. Reports put the estimated value of the property at around Rs 100 crore, although the figure has not been independently confirmed.Vadivelu’s new house features traditional Tamil architectureUnlike a modern home built around glass walls and flashy designs, Vadivelu’s new house reportedly follows a traditional architectural style. According to Filmibeat, one of its key features is a thinnai, the raised seating area commonly found at the entrance of old Tamil homes. The space offers visitors a place to sit and spend time. A small statue of Lord Ganesha is also present at the property, which gives a devotional touch. The house seems to be a combination of traditional Tamil architecture while offering the comfort of a modern home. The large outdoor space also helps guests sit comfortably when they come to meet the actor.Solar panels, CCTV, and a private office among Vadivelu house amenitiesThe property is said to include a number of amenities for the convenience and safety of the occupants. Solar panels have been installed to meet the energy requirement, while the inverter works as a backup during a power cut. CCTV cameras are also included in the security system. The house also has a dedicated parking space for cars, making it easy to park vehicles. Another important amenity the house offers is an office located on the property itself.Vadivelu’s new home has a garden with fruit treesGreen spaces are another feature of the actor’s new residence. The garden reportedly includes sapodilla, banana, gooseberry, coconut and jackfruit plants. These trees give the outdoor area a natural setting and add to the traditional atmosphere of the property. With its greenery, open space and classic front verandah, this house is quite unique and stands out from the regular city houses. After returning to film through "Naai Sekar Returns," Vadivelu performed in movies like 'Chandramukhi 2,' 'Maamannan,' and 'Maareesan.' Through his performances in 'Maamannan' and 'Maareesan,' Vadivelu introduced a new side of himself as an actor to his fans that did not revolve around the typical comedian roles he is known for. articles.title: Christina Applegate Breaks Down in Tears Revealing She Was Misdiagnosed with MS: ‘I’m Back at Square One’
articles.summary: Applegate shared the shocking news on the ‘MeSsy’ podcast after seven months away
articles.body:
Christina Applegate learned from her doctor that she does not have multiple sclerosis despite experiencing debilitating symptoms since 2021

The actress said if anything her condition has gotten worse and doctors will investigate what has caused her health issues

Applegate returned to MeSsy podcast after taking time away to process the diagnosis change and other health concerns

Christina Applegate returned to hosting her MeSsy podcast with shocking news.

On Tuesday, Oct. 20, Applegate and co-host Jamie Lynn Sigler released back-to-back episodes of their podcast, where the actresses have raw discussions about their respective journeys with multiple sclerosis.

However, during her return episode Applegate, 54, emotionally shared that she's taken time away from the podcast to process a new revelation from her doctor — she does not, in fact, have MS.

"She came into my room and said, 'Congratulations, you don't have MS,' " Applegate recalled through tears. "I was, like, not happy at all. Everybody else was so happy."

Dr. Marwa Kaisey, associate professor with the Cedars-Sinai Medical Center department of neurology, who joined Applegate and Sigler for the second episode of the podcast, says MS misdiagnoses are "fairly common" due to the fact that "we don't have one single test for MS. It's not like we have something like a pregnancy test that says, 'Yes. You have it.' 'No. You don't.' It's a list of criteria." Kaisey says nearly 20 percent of those diagnosed with MS turn out not to have the disease. "Almost one in five of these people who'd been told they had MS, some for decades, didn't actually have it. And a majority of them were on medication to treat their MS."

Applegate noted that despite learning that she'd been misdiagnosed, it didn't impact any of her debilitating symptoms.

"You don't get misdiagnosed and then all of the sudden I'm better," Applegate continued. "I haven't gotten better, Jamie! If anything, I've gotten worse. So I'm back at square one where I don't know what's going on with me. And that's going to be an online investigation that my doctors are going to be getting into just to find out what has been going on since 2021, why did this happen?"

In the Part II of the podcast, Applegate once again got emotional, saying, "I've gone through a great depression because of it. But I lost everything. I lost my job. I lost — I'm sorry. What do you say to someone who's been living with this for six years — God, I'm so sorry — because it stopped my life. I still have to use wheelchairs when I go to the doctor's office. I can't walk from the car to the room. I'm still in this. Nothing magical happened when she said, 'You don't have MS.' Nothing magical happened."

The Dead to Me actress admitted to struggling with her place in the MS community, especially after building a community of others who were diagnosed with MS.

"It's weird because I feel like I let everybody down," Applegate shared. "It's this weird feeling because I became this — you and I, the poster children for MS. And everything I was doing. I had a reason. I had a f---ing reason as to why my day sucked every day. And now I don't have a reason and it's very unnerving and it's very confusing for me."

Applegate said she's still in a "state of shock" over the misdiagnosis, calling it a "mindf---."

The Emmy winner added that she took time off from the podcast to "process" the news while also experiencing "some health stuff."

Ultimately, Applegate shared that she views her health journey as, "the same game with a different name."

The Emmy Award-winning actress' last appearance on the podcast was in March.

On March 31, Sigler announced that the pair were taking a short hiatus from MeSsy . Shortly after, it was reported that Applegate had been hospitalized due to complications of her multiple sclerosis. The podcast resumed on April 21 and Sigler spent the following months recording episodes solo while featuring special guests.

Applegate was originally diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2021. The progressive disease damages the protective cover around nerves, called myelin, in the central nervous system, according to the Cleveland Clinic . It can cause muscle weakness, vision changes, numbness, memory loss and gastrointestinal issues.

The actress first addressed reports of her hospitalization via Instagram in April, shortly following the release of her memoir, You With the Sad Eyes . She thanked fans for their support and added, "Health issues are a constant for me, but I'm a strong chick and I'm getting stronger and better every day."

"I'm taking a moment to focus on my health, but I'll be back with more to say soon enough," she said at the time.

In August, a source told PEOPLE that she was home from the hospital and "doing very well."

articles.title: Bappi Lahiri honored: Sangeetkar Bappi Lahiri Marg inaugurated; family and fans celebrate the late composer's legacy
articles.summary: Around five decades of memories, music and milestones came together in Juhu on Monday evening as the road leading to the late singer-composer Bappi
articles.body: Around five decades of memories, music and milestones came together in Juhu on Monday evening as the road leading to the late singer-composer Bappi Lahiri’s residence was named Sangeetkar Bappi Lahiri Marg. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis inaugurated the road in the presence of the Lahiri family, members of the film and music fraternity, and well-wishers, honouring a musician whose distinctive sound continues to resonate with audiences.For the family, the occasion was deeply personal. Bappi Lahiri’s wife, Chitrani Lahiri, son Bappa Lahiri and his wife Taneesha, grandsons Krrish and Shivaay, daughter Reema Lahiri Bansal, son-in-law Govind Bansal and grandson Swastik Bansal, popularly known as Rego B, were present at the ceremony.Speaking exclusively to Bombay Times, Bappa Lahiri said, “My dad was just 15 when he came to Mumbai. He would always say that Kolkata was his janmabhoomi and Maharashtra his karmabhoomi. We have lived in this house and this lane for more than four decades now, and almost all of his hits were created here. The mural I designed for this road combines a record and musical waves, depicting his musical journey.”His sister Reema echoed the family's pride and emotion at the tribute. “This is a big honour for our dad, who was a legend. We are all very emotional, but also proud and happy. My grandparents, Aparesh and Bansari Lahiri, are also blessing us today. Even now, my father's hit music can be heard everywhere, whether in Dhurandhar or Baaghi,” she said.Known for pioneering a distinctive blend of disco, pop and Indian film music, Bappi Lahiri enjoyed a career spanning decades, creating songs that became enduring favourites across generations. His flamboyant persona and signature gold accessories made him as recognisable as his music, earning him a unique place in popular culture.The ceremony saw several familiar faces from the film and music industries come together to pay tribute to the composer. Among those present were Jeetendra, Jackie Shroff, Udit Narayan, Ashoke Pandit, Ila Arun, Poonam Dhillon, Rohit Roy, Alisha Chinai, Anu Malik, Rajat Bedi, Sofie Choudhary, Lalit Pandit and Neetu Chandra.Jackie Shroff’s presence also drew attention as it came a day after a firing incident involving his son, actor Tiger Shroff.For the Lahiri family, the newly named road is more than a civic landmark. It is a tribute rooted in the neighbourhood that witnessed the making of the composer's music and the life he built in Mumbai; a lasting reminder of an artist whose melodies continue to find new listeners.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Taylor Swift reclaimed her first six albums in 2025; a 2026 music-rights deal involving two of her biggest hits revealed another layer of the songwriting business
articles.summary: Taylor Swift’s 2025 purchase of the master recordings of her first six albums marked a significant moment in her long-running fight for control over her
articles.body: Taylor Swift’s 2025 purchase of the master recordings of her first six albums marked a significant moment in her long-running fight for control over her music. However, a separate transaction announced in June 2026 has highlighted another side of the music business, the ownership of songwriting and publishing rights. HarbourView Equity Partners acquired the publisher’s share of selected compositions written by Wolf Cousins, the songwriting collective founded by Swedish hitmakers Max Martin and Shellback. The deal included two Swift hits, Style and …Ready for It?. It did not affect Swift’s existing ownership of the recordings or transfer her own songwriting share. Instead, it demonstrated how different rights associated with the same song can belong to different parties.How the 2026 deal involved two Taylor Swift hitsOn June 24, 2026, HarbourView announced a strategic partnership with Wolf Cousins and confirmed that it had acquired the publisher’s share of selected compositions written by the collective. Founded by Max Martin and Shellback, Wolf Cousins has been involved in creating commercially successful songs across pop music.The compositions covered by the deal included Swift’s Style, from her 2014 album 1989, and …Ready for It?, from her 2017 album Reputation. Both songs were co-written by Swift, Martin and Shellback.The transaction also included songs recorded by other artists, including Ariana Grande’s Problem, Into You and No Tears Left to Cry; The Weeknd’s Can’t Feel My Face; Imagine Dragons’ Believer; Ellie Goulding’s Love Me Like You Do; Tove Lo’s Habits (Stay High); and DNCE’s Cake by the Ocean. Warner Chappell continues to administer the catalogue, according to HarbourView’s announcement.The financial terms were not publicly disclosed by HarbourView. Variety, which first reported the transaction, cited sources who placed its value in the low nine figures. The investment firm declined to confirm that figure, so it should be treated as a reported valuation rather than an officially established sale price.What is the difference between master recordings and publishing rights?The distinction between the two types of rights is central to understanding the transaction.A master recording refers to a specific recorded version of a song. The underlying musical composition, meanwhile, consists of the music and lyrics. A single track can therefore involve separate copyright interests held by recording owners, songwriters and music publishers.Master rights can generate revenue when a particular recording is streamed, sold or licensed. Publishing rights can generate royalties when the underlying composition is performed publicly, reproduced or licensed for certain uses, including film and television productions.In Swift’s case, the 2026 transaction concerned the publisher’s share of selected compositions associated with Martin and Shellback. It did not mean that HarbourView acquired Swift’s original recordings or her own share of the songwriting copyright. The transaction illustrates how an investor can acquire one part of a song’s rights without owning the entire work.Why music publishing attracts investorsEstablished songwriting catalogues can offer investors income from several sources. These include royalties associated with streaming, public performances and the licensing of compositions for films, television programmes and advertisements.The appeal also lies in the potential longevity of successful songs. A composition can continue generating revenue years after its release, particularly when it remains popular or finds new audiences through films, television, social media and other uses.Fortune quoted Barry Massarsky, who leads music and entertainment valuation services at advisory firm Citrin Cooperman, explaining that established catalogues can be attractive because their earnings become easier to evaluate as their revenue patterns stabilise. Massarsky was not involved in the HarbourView transaction.Ownership of publishing rights can also affect licensing negotiations. When a company acquires a songwriter’s share, it may reduce the number of separate parties that need to be consulted for certain uses. However, other rights holders may still need to grant permission, depending on the ownership structure and the intended use.How Taylor Swift regained her first six albumsSwift’s 2025 acquisition followed years of disputes over the ownership of her early recordings.She signed with Big Machine Label Group as a teenager, and the label retained the master recordings of her first six albums. In 2019, music manager Scooter Braun acquired Big Machine, bringing the masters under his control. The recordings were subsequently sold to investment firm Shamrock Capital in 2020.Swift responded by re-recording four of the albums: Fearless (Taylor’s Version), Red (Taylor’s Version), Speak Now (Taylor’s Version) and 1989 (Taylor’s Version). The new recordings gave her versions of the songs that she owned, while the original masters remained separately owned.On May 30, 2025, Swift announced that she had purchased the original master recordings from Shamrock Capital. Her statement also referred to associated music videos, concert films, album artwork, photography and unreleased songs. She thanked Shamrock for the transaction and described the acquisition as a long-held personal goal. The financial terms were not disclosed.Why the 2026 deal does not reverse Swift’s 2025 achievementSwift’s acquisition gave her ownership of the original master recordings of her first six albums, but it did not automatically give her every share of the underlying compositions written with collaborators.The HarbourView transaction involved the publishing interests associated with Martin and Shellback’s contributions to selected songs. Swift’s own songwriting interests were not reported as part of the sale, and the transaction did not undo her acquisition of the masters.The distinction is particularly relevant to songs that have been re-recorded. Publishing rights relate to the underlying composition, meaning they can apply to different recordings of the same song, subject to the relevant rights and agreements. Consequently, a publisher’s interest in a composition can remain commercially valuable even when an artist owns a particular recording of it.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Spotify’s new podcast memberships let you pay for extra perks
articles.summary: Spotify is enabling podcast creators to earn more money through the platform by providing their fans with a way to pay to access exclusive content.
articles.body: Spotify is enabling podcast creators to earn more money through the platform by providing their fans with a way to pay to access exclusive content. First announced in May, the new Memberships subscription feature is starting to roll out in 34 regions today, allowing podcasters to offer perks including additional content, early access, bonus episodes, and reduced ads behind a paywall. Users can find Memberships on a podcast’s Spotify page, with the ability to subscribe, pay, and access the exclusive benefits “in just a few taps,” according to Spotify. Podcast creators can set their pricing options and bundle benefits across multiple subscription tiers, and keep 90 percent of membership revenue. Spotify is providing podcasters with tools to analyze and build their Memberships audience, including targeted promotions and free trial offers, alongside community engagement features like member badges, welcome clips, and more. That makes this more like a Patreon-style membership system in which fans can choose to give additional support to their favorite creators, and is distinct from the podcast subscription feature that Spotify introduced in 2021. Podcasters can utilize Memberships alongside other Spotify revenue streams, including ads and the Spotify Partner Program. To qualify for Memberships, shows must be hosted on Spotify for Creators or Megaphone, and have at least 100 consumption hours, 100 listeners or viewers, and three published episodes. Spotify is also making it easy for podcasters who manage their subscriptions on other services to try Memberships, allowing them to bring their paywalled content to Spotify via its Open Access feature.

articles.title: Apu vuelve a 'Los Simpson' tras su marcha en 2017: "Estamos entusiasmados"
articles.standfirst: El actor Sunil Malhotra pondrá voz al popular personaje de la serie
articles.summary: El actor Sunil Malhotra pondrá voz al popular personaje de la serie
articles.body: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon, el popular personaje de la serie de animación 'Los Simpson' que regenta una tienda de 24 horas (el badulaque, como lo denominan en sus capítulos), vuelve. La última que los seguidores de la serie habían oído a Apu fue en 2017. Concretamente, en el episodio 'Los Serfson'. Desde entonces, Apu no había tenido voz. Esto cambiará. El actor de doblaje, en su versión original, será Sunil Malhotra, que ha participado en 'Anatomía de Grey' o 'La leyenda de Korra', será el encargado de dar voz a Apu Nahasapeemapetilon en el episodio 'La Venganza', emitido el pasado domingo, según ha informado Variety. El productor ejecutivo Matt Selman confesó, en declaraciones recogidas por el citado medio, la importancia de Apu en la serie y aplaudió la incorporación de Sunil Malhotra. "Nos encanta este personaje y queríamos traerlo de vuelta de una forma inteligente, al estilo de 'Los Simpson', que le permitiera evolucionar. Estamos entusiasmados con lo que Sunil ya ha aportado al papel y esperamos ver más de Apu en el futuro", explicó. El regreso de Apu va más allá de una simple cuestión argumental. El documental 'The Problem With Apu', en 2017, puso de relieve el polémico doblaje del personaje, al que entonces ponía voz Hank Azaria. Algunos consideraron que el acento que le otorgaba al personaje podían contribuir a incrementar los estereotipos sobre los ciudadanos de origen indio. De hecho, hasta el propio Azaria, como recuerda Variety, pidió disculpas de forma pública: "Una parte de mí siente la necesidad de ir a cada persona de origen indio en este país y disculparme personalmente. Y a veces lo hago". Nueve años después, Apu Nahasapeemapetilon regresa a la serie de animación más popular de la televisión. Los responsables de 'Los Simpson' confían en que la aportación del nuevo actor Sunil Malhotra sea clave en el nuevo enfoque del personaje en los próximos capítulos. El artista se ha mostrado emocionado por esta nueva etapa.

articles.title: Alderney fisherman concerned over falling fish numbers
articles.summary: The comments come after the island's fishing festival, with many species seen in fewer numbers.
articles.body:
An angler has raised concerns around Alderney's declining fish population, following the island's 38th annual fishing festival.

More than 70 anglers from across the Bailiwick of Guernsey and the UK competed in the Alderney Fishing Festival last week.

But David Nash, a local fisherman and former journalist, said conger, bass, mackerel, pollock, and garfish were "very, very few" in number compared with previous years.

The festival's committee said whilst fishing "was certainly tougher than usual", there were still some good fish caught and populations and species "seem to fluctuate from year to year".

According to Nash, the people who got involved fished with "great intensity" for the whole week.

He said: "It was great, but there were certain species that over the last two or three years have been on the decline, like conger and bass, which were very, very few."

Nash said: "We only had two decent bass weighed this year, two big congers, and very few mackerel this year."

The temperature of the water and there being more seals made a difference, he said.

"What most of the anglers were talking about was that the water is very, very warm at the moment - it's climate change.

"There's also been a growth in the seal population here on Burhou Island, which keeps chasing the fish out into deeper, colder water."

Despite this, Nash was positive about the future of the festival, with eight junior anglers taking part.

"We've had a fantastically successful competition this year," he said.

In a statement, James Clark, the president of the Alderney Fishing Festival committee said: "Whilst fishing was certainly tougher than usual during the festival, there were still some good fish caught and the qualifying board ended up around 75% full.

"Fish populations and species seem to fluctuate from year to year, with some species being more abundant in certain years and less abundant in others.

"We're very pleased with the support from our anglers and appreciate how many people entered the festival."

articles.title: Wii Sports is back on the Switch 2, and it rules
articles.summary: Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a continuation of the Wii Sports series, bringing motion-controlled bowling and tennis to the Switch 2.
articles.body: Wii Sports holds an important place in Nintendo’s history. It’s the best-selling piece of software the company has ever made, one that permeated culture in surprising ways, and its success helped rejuvenate Nintendo after a period of steady decline. It also kicked off one of the company’s most important and unassuming franchises. While subsequent sports titles from Nintendo never sold quite as well as the original Wii Sports, they’ve become a fixture for each new console, much like a new Mario Kart or Pokémon. And now the Switch 2 has its own version, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort, and it’s the best so far. You’d be forgiven for not realizing that Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is launching this week. The game is coming out during a particularly hectic time for new video game releases, and it’s sandwiched between two flashier Switch 2 titles in Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave and the upcoming remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Amid all of that, it’s easy to forget a game about thumb wrestling and bowling. But Sports Resort is also a refined and expansive version of the concept, and one that will likely become a constant over the Switch 2’s life. The core of the game is the same as always: giving you a bunch of athletic activities — they’re not exactly all “sports” — that require some form of motion controls to play. That means swinging a Joy-Con controller to simulate using a tennis racket or tossing a bowling ball. There are 12 sports in all, and they vary quite a bit. The aforementioned returning favorites tennis and bowling are joined by things like skateboarding, thumb wrestling, and flying a plane. [Image: What makes the game work is its simplicity. Almost each activity is incredibly easy to pick up; I don’t know much about golf, but it only took me a minute or so to get down the fundamentals of swinging a club using a Joy-Con. This means that Sports Resort excels as an arcade-style experience, the kind of game you pull out when friends are over and you want to have some fun. Thumb wrestling is ideal for this. It’s so simple — you move your hand back and forth and use a single button to try and “pin” your opponent — yet gets extremely intense and fun in the competitive two-player mode. And unlike IRL thumb wrestling, no one can actually cheat. There are some exceptions to the general simplicity. I still find basketball to be a little too complex, and I just can’t seem to figure out a successful strategy in table tennis. But there are enough games in Sports Resort that you’re almost certain to find a handful of favorites you’ll stick with, so having a few duds isn’t the end of the world. There’s also a decent amount of depth, both in terms of the skill ceiling for games — I have spent hours trying to perfect the spin on my bowling release — but also the various modes for each sport. Bowling, for instance, includes the returning option to play with 100 pins at once, which is chaotic as it sounds. But the biggest addition to Sports Resort is that it now takes place in an open world. That may sound strange for a collection of arcade games, but it also allows it to introduce three new activities that are centered on exploring the beautiful island setting. There’s prop plane (where you hold the Joy-Con like a paper airplane to fly), power cruising (where you hold two Joy-Con horizontally, like the handlebars of a Jet Ski), and skateboarding (where you use the Joy-Con’s mouse controls to simulate controlling a tiny skateboard). There are competitive ways to play these games, like a skateboard race, but I’ve spent most of my time with a sightseeing mode where the goal is to find as many landmarks and secrets across the resort as you can within a five-minute time limit. It’s sort of like a more fleshed-out version of the free roam mode in Mario Kart World. The island is surprisingly detailed and interesting to explore, with lots of caves and hidden paths, and the three modes of transportation let you check it out via land, water, and air. [Image: These exploration-focused modes add a nice new dimension to the experience, fitting snugly within the more traditional sports while offering a very different vibe. I’ve become particularly drawn to skateboarding — there’s something very satisfying about pulling back on the Joy-Con to simulate pushing a board — especially since you can collect items that let you purchase new clothes and other accessories to customize your character. One of the biggest keys to Nintendo’s success during the Switch era has been consistency. Even in the midst of a tumultuous period for the broader games industry, the company has managed to put out a steady stream of games, many of which have had a surprisingly long life. Nintendo’s biggest hits aren’t always what you expect. The first Nintendo Switch Sports has sold more than 18 million copies, topping beloved games like Super Mario Bros. Wonder and Splatoon 3. A little over a year into its existence, that style of perennial seller is exactly what the Switch 2 needs, the kind of game that people pick up alongside Mario Kart when they buy a new console. Wii Sports showed just how transformative a game like that can be, and Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is quietly keeping that spirit alive. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort launches on the Switch 2 on October 22nd.

articles.title: Christina Applegate says she was misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis
articles.summary: Christina Applegate announced Tuesday that she had been misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis.
articles.body: Emmy-nominated actor Christina Applegate announced Tuesday that she had been misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis, a condition she believed she had for more than five years, leaving her “back at square one” as she continues to experience debilitating medical issues. Applegate, who revealed the misdiagnosis on the latest episode of her podcast “MeSsy,” broke down in tears as she recalled a doctor recently telling her: “Congratulations. You don’t have MS.” She said that she was “not happy at all” about the news. “You don’t get misdiagnosed and then all of a sudden I’m better,” Applegate told her podcast co-host, “The Sopranos” actor Jamie-Lynn Sigler. “I haven’t gotten better, Jamie. If anything, I’ve gotten worse in some ways. “I’m back at square one, that I don’t know what’s going on with me,” said Applegate, who spent months in the hospital earlier this year and recently took a break from co-hosting “MeSsy” with Sigler, who was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis roughly 25 years ago. Applegate disclosed that she had been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2021, calling her medical ordeal “a tough road.” She received a standing ovation at the 2024 Emmy Awards, appearing on stage with a cane. In an interview that year, she said she lived “kind of in hell.” Multiple sclerosis is a progressive disease of the central nervous system that disrupts the flow of information between the brain and body. The immune system attacks the body’s nerve linings, producing unpredictable symptoms such as pain, fatigue or paralysis. In the two-part podcast episode released Tuesday, Applegate said the lack of clarity about her medical condition was “unnerving” and “confusing.” “It’s weird because I feel like I let everybody down,” Applegate told Sigler. “It’s this weird feeling because I became this — you and I — the poster children for MS. ... I had a f---ing reason as to why my day sucked every day.” She said her medical team will work to determine the underlying cause of her symptoms. “Why did this happen? I had every symptom of someone with MS. Every single one,” Applegate said. Applegate is best known for her television roles on Fox’s “Married with Children” and Netflix’s “Dead to Me.” She also appeared in both “Anchorman” movies as TV news anchor Veronica Corningstone. She has received eight Emmy nominations, winning in 2003 for her guest appearance on NBC’s “Friends.”

articles.title: Spotify pulled 50 million AI slop and spam tracks from its recommendations
articles.summary: Spotify says it has removed more than 50 million songs identified as AI slop or spam from its music recommendations.
articles.body: Spotify says it has removed more than 50 million songs considered AI-generated slop or spam from user recommendations over the past year. That’s according to an announcement on Tuesday that says Spotify has also made changes to its recommendation system to highlight more music made by human artists. “Our editors hold the same standard and don’t program content identified as slop or spam,” Spotify says. “Since we made these changes, we’ve seen a marked decrease in listener concerns about this content showing up in recommendations.” Though Spotify has stopped short of mandating labels on all AI tracks, it launched an “AI Persona” badge for artists that use an AI identity and don’t represent a real person. It also won’t recommend music from AI personas. Other music streaming platforms are taking a tougher stance on AI music, with YouTube Music putting labels on AI songs, Deezer giving users an option to filter out AI slop, and Bandcamp banning AI music entirely. Spotify says it uses a combination of listener engagement and feedback, upload patterns, metadata, and third-party AI detection tools to determine whether a track may be AI-generated slop. Last year, the company said it took down more than 75 million songs identified as spam. It’s also partnering with Universal Music Group and the independent music publisher Believe to launch a tool for creating AI music remixes.

articles.title: Over $963,000 worth of graded Pokémon and sports cards were stolen from FedEx
articles.summary: Last week several packages of graded collectible cards valued at around $963,000 were stolen from a FedEx truck as they were being shipped back to their owners.
articles.body: Last week over 200 packages of graded trading cards being shipped back to their owners were stolen from a FedEx truck parked outside the headquarters of Professional Sports Authenticator (PSA) in Santa Ana, California, according to a report by The Athletic. PSA is one of the largest third-party sports and hobby card grading companies in the world and it reported to the Santa Ana Police Department that the majority of the stolen packages had an approximate value of over $963,000, but that amount could further increase as PSA continues the process of confirming exactly which cards included in the shipment were taken. In a statement shared to its website, Collectors Holdings, the parent company of PSA, acknowledged the theft and that it’s working closely with local law enforcement and FedEx as the investigation continues. In response to the incident the company says it has “notified marketplace partners so they can be on the lookout for rare and serialized items” to help prevent the stolen cards from being resold. All cards graded by PSA are assigned a unique certification number that the company has since deactivated for all the cards that have so far been identified as stolen. Collectors Holdings also says it has contacted affected customers to arrange compensation based on the fair market value of their missing collectibles, but “up to the maximum insured value for each item selected by the customer prior to grading,” according to the report. [Media: In a video posted over the weekend, YouTuber Sky-B Cards identified themselves as one of the victims of the theft and shared the response they were sent by PSA. They had paid $8,468 to have 104 collectible sports cards graded by the company, many of which are irreplaceable, and had opted to insure the order for up to $156,000. It is not yet known what compensation they have received. Other collectors affected by the incident have started to reach out to another YouTuber, Boston Card Hunter, who is working to compile a shared list of serialized cards that were stolen including detailed descriptions of each one in hopes it can help other collectors identify them.

articles.title: Roman 'curse' tablets on show at Cirencester Corinium Museum
articles.summary: The tablets, used by Romans to target those who had wronged them, are going on show for first time
articles.body:
A rare set of Roman 'curse' stone tablets are going on show in the UK for the first time.

Visitors to the Corinium Museum in Cirencester will have the opportunity to preview the exhibition of the tablets, which were found in the Cotswolds and have been loaned to the museum by the Research I Library in the USA for the next five years.

The tablets were used by Romans, who were deeply superstitious, to try and negatively influence the lives of those who had wronged them.

They will be available to view for the first time during the Cirencester History Festival, which runs from 23 October to 1 November 2026.

Corinium Museum director Emma Stuart said that the tablets are the "first example of this type of artefact we have from the Roman period" and described them as a "wonderful example of Roman revenge".

"Unlike the Roman Baths, we didn't have any examples of curse tablets in our collection until the generous offer was made by Research I Library," she added.

"It's always great to have things in the museum that have been found here, but curse tablets are very rare", said Phillip Brant-Simmons, collections and engagement assistant at the museum.

"It's amazing for us to have even a small piece of this history.

"They're so different from anything else we have in the museum and it's great that people are now getting the opportunity to see them."

The museum will also host a Halloween workshop for children to 'make their own curse tablets' on 31 October.

articles.body: Alex Cooper, the host of “Call Her Daddy,” is now a mom. Cooper, 32, announced the birth of her first child, a boy, in an Instagram post Tuesday. According to the American Diabetes Association, gestational diabetes can affect up to 9% of pregnancies. Kaplan, a Hollywood producer, married Cooper in April 2024. articles.title: Top baby names heading into 2027 inspired by ‘The Odyssey,’ ‘Yellowstone’ and ‘Heated Rivalry’
articles.summary: BabyCenter released the most popular baby names of 2026 and the trends it expects to shape 2027, including “The Odyssey,” “Yellowstone” and “Heated Rivalry.”
articles.body: Somewhere in a delivery room, a new parent is weighing a name that sounds like a Greek hero, a Montana ranch hand or a brooding hockey player from a streaming series. According to BabyCenter’s latest data, they’re far from alone. BabyCenter, a digital parenting resource that’s been reporting on baby names and trends for more than 20 years, just released its annual lists of the most popular baby names of 2026 and the trends it expects to shape 2027. The findings, shared with NBC News, draw on more than 350,000 babies born this year to parents registered on the BabyCenter app. Because parents submit names in real time, the company can predict trends before the Social Security Administration releases its official list. At the very top, little has changed from last year. Noah and Olivia both keep their No. 1 spots. Just beneath them, though, one name is making a lot of noise. Eliana has shot up to No. 2 for girls, a remarkable climb from No. 14 in 2024 and No. 7 last year. BabyCenter’s baby name advisor, Steph Coffield, calls it the year’s most surprising trend and predicts that if the momentum holds, Eliana could take the top girls’ spot next year. If there’s a theme running through this year’s data, it’s with that first letter E. E is the most popular starting initial for girls, making up 15% of the top 100 girls’ names. For boys, J leads, with 14% of the top 100. The E-names are having a moment well beyond the top 10. Elsie rose 23 spots, Evangeline 50, Elodie 87, Elaine 143 and Esme a whopping 222. Among the boys, Josiah surged 33 spots to No. 21 and Jeremiah climbed 28 spots to reach No. 60, while Jaxon, Jaxson and Jasper all hold spots in the top 100. Scroll further down the list and you’ll find some fresh faces. Magnolia is the only brand-new girls’ name. But on the boys’ side, Stetson, Archer and Milo all debuted, joined by Dean, which is making its first top 100 appearance this century after a heyday in the ’50s and ’60s. Length is trending upward, too. Nearly three in 10 of the top girls’ names and 31% of the top boys’ names have seven or more letters. The longest name in the mix is Christopher, at 11. Many of those longer, bolder picks are coming straight from the screen, and nowhere is that clearer than on the ice. In the same year ESPN logged its most-watched NHL playoff season, ice-rink TV dramas, including “Off Campus” and “Heated Rivalry,” sent names like Garrett, Allie, Beau and Jules climbing. The breakout star is Ilya, which rocketed up more than 6,000 spots to No. 2,197 for boys. Trade the rink for the open range, and another small-screen hit is leaving its mark. The lingering pull of “Yellowstone,” with its cowboy hats, boots and line dancing, is carrying into the nursery. As mentioned earlier, Stetson rose 46 spots to No. 95, the first time it has ever cracked BabyCenter’s top 100. Walker (up 19), Callahan (up 88), Wilder (up 107) and Gunner (up 151) are riding the same wave. But the cowboys have some competition from across the sea. Names from Greek mythology are washing ashore, boosted by the blockbuster movie “The Odyssey.” Boys’ names on the rise include Atlas (up 5), Orion and Troy (both up 9), Ares (up 32), Evander (up 128) and Perseus (up 249). For girls, Iris (up 18), Lydia (up 38) and Daphne (up 42) are climbing. “The trends this year show parents are ready to dig into the archives with some modern appreciation for the ancient, the vintage, the classic,” Coffield said. In some cases, that archive is a cozy Connecticut town. With a “Gilmore Girls” documentary newly announced, fall rewatches are sending Stars Hollow names soaring. Lorelai is up 12 spots and Rory up 31. Among the boys, Christopher is up 4, Luke up 7, Richard up 29 and Dean up 31, which helps explain that name’s return to the top 100. Not every name is riding the pop culture wave, though, and one has had a rough year. Between Taylor Swift’s wedding, Taylor Farms’ lettuce recalls and a two famous Taylors welcoming a baby with Taylor as the middle name, BabyCenter says parents are over it. For girls, Taylor dropped 24 spots to No. 399. For boys, it plummeted 262 spots to No. 1,093, falling out of the top 1,000 for the first time ever. So back to that delivery room. Whatever name new parents are landing on, whether it’s a mythic hero, a rugged cowboy or a Stars Hollow favorite, chances are it’s already climbing the charts.

articles.title: JustWatch now streams TV shows and movies, too
articles.summary: JustWatch TV’s new streaming service launched today with both ad-supported free tiers and paid subscriptions with exclusive added features.
articles.body: After announcing plans to introduce its own streaming service last month, JustWatch, a popular guide and search engine for finding things to watch on existing platforms like Disney Plus and Netflix, launched JustWatch TV today. The new streaming service offers an ad-supported free subscription, an ad-free paid subscription, and movie rentals with content from 30 global partners. The streaming service is accessible through JustWatch’s existing mobile apps and its website and is currently available in 12 markets including the US, Canada, France, Italy, Australia, and the UK. Content providers include Bleecker Street, Cineverse, Fremantle, New Regency, and Paramount, as well as region-specific partners around the world. Three options will be available to those who sign up. JustWatch TV Free includes a “curated selection of titles” available with ads, while the paid JustWatch TV Plus subscription has over 300 ad-free titles plus other exclusive app features like the ability to hide shows you’ve disliked or already watched in its guide. The JustWatch TV Store will include a “growing selection of recent and popular movies to rent” but is initially only available in the US, UK, Ireland, Australia, and New Zealand. JustWatch TV Plus will be priced at $3.99 per month and include a 10 percent discount on rentals, but the company is also offering a $49.99 lifetime subscription. Even if the price of the content it provides increases, the company believes the value of the data it collects will still make the lifetime subscription option worth it, according to TechCrunch.

articles.title: Mariah Carey wins as judge dismisses brother Morgan Carey’s defamation lawsuit seeking $20 million over memoir ‘The Meaning of Mariah Carey’; court cites failure to prove actual malice, lawyer to appeal
articles.summary: Mariah Carey has won a legal battle against her brother, Morgan Carey, after a judge dismissed his defamation lawsuit over the singer’s 2020 memoir, The
articles.body: Mariah Carey has won a legal battle against her brother, Morgan Carey, after a judge dismissed his defamation lawsuit over the singer’s 2020 memoir, The Meaning of Mariah Carey. According to reports by Rolling Stone and TheWrap, Morgan had alleged that the book damaged his reputation by portraying him as a violent drug dealer with a criminal history, seeking more than $20 million in damages.The New York judge dismissed Morgan’s remaining defamation claims on October 19, 2026, ruling that he had failed to establish that Mariah knew the statements were false or had recklessly disregarded the truth. The court found that his allegations did not meet the high legal threshold required to prove defamation involving matters of public interest.The $20 million figure refers to the damages Morgan claimed in the lawsuit; it was not an amount awarded by the court. Following the dismissal, his lawyer indicated that he intended to appeal the decision.Why Morgan Carey sued Mariah Carey over her memoirMorgan, who is 10 years older than the singer, filed the lawsuit in 2021. He alleged that the memoir portrayed him as a violent drug dealer who had “been in the system”. He insisted that he was neither violent nor had a criminal record.Morgan also claimed that the book had severely damaged his reputation and affected his ability to secure work. He described himself as having been “ruined” by the memoir, which referred to him as her “ex-brother”. According to his allegations, he lost professional opportunities and struggled to find steady employment following its publication.He also argued that Mariah had failed to fact-check the passages concerning him with him before the book was released.However, Mariah’s legal team argued that the failure to consult Morgan before publication did not, by itself, establish the “actual malice” required for a defamation claim.Earlier court ruling allowed some claims to proceedThe latest decision follows an earlier ruling in 2022, when Judge Barbara Jaffe dismissed 14 of the 16 claims in Morgan’s original complaint and rejected all claims against the book’s publisher.However, Jaffe allowed certain allegations involving claims that Morgan had distributed cocaine in the 1980s and had “been in the system” to proceed against Mariah.The judge also found that other statements in the memoir, including allegations that Morgan had been abusive and had accepted money to murder someone, could potentially be defamatory. However, Morgan had failed to adequately establish that he suffered damages from those statements.Morgan’s attorneys appealed the ruling, arguing that the trial court had not considered the full context of the memoir. The decision was subsequently upheld.Morgan Carey’s lawyer plans another appealFollowing the latest dismissal, Morgan’s attorney, Richard Roth, said he intended to challenge the decision again.In an email quoted in earlier reporting, Roth criticised the ruling for disregarding the earlier decision that had allowed certain statements to form the basis of a defamation claim.“In rendering its decision, the Court literally ignored the prior decision from Justice Jaffe, that specifically held the statements were sufficient to defeat a motion to dismiss, which decision was affirmed by the First Department,” Roth said.“So, we will go up to the First Department on appeal.”The planned appeal could extend the legal dispute, which began shortly after the publication of Mariah’s memoir in 2020.Mariah Carey’s sister Alison also filed a lawsuit over the memoirMorgan was not the only member of the Carey family to raise legal objections to the memoir. Their sister, Alison Carey, filed a separate defamation lawsuit, alleging that the book falsely portrayed her as having thrown boiling tea on Mariah and having “tried to pimp her out”.However, Alison’s lawsuit was never pursued. She died in 2024.Mariah’s memoir, The Meaning of Mariah Carey, was published in 2020 and detailed the singer’s life, career and complicated family relationships. Morgan’s lawsuit centred on passages he claimed were false and damaging. The judge’s latest decision dismisses his remaining claims, although his lawyer has said he intends to appeal. articles.summary: Erik von Detten faces financial elder abuse and fraud allegations after an elderly couple claims they lost over $900,000 on overpriced gold coins.
articles.body: Former Disney star Erik von Detten is being sued by an elderly California couple who claim he convinced them to invest more than $2.1 million of their retirement savings in overpriced gold coins. Sheila Greenberg, 85, and her husband, Norman Greenberg, 97, filed the lawsuit against von Detten, who is best known for his roles in Disney's "Brink" and "The Princess Diaries," and his former employer, Rosland Capital, in Los Angeles County Superior Court on May 11. The complaint accuses the defendants of financial elder abuse, fraud, breach of fiduciary duty, constructive fraud and conversion. According to court documents obtained by Fox News Digital, the Greenbergs believe Rosland "designed in large part to appeal to senior citizens through their television and internet advertising, direct mail brochures, and high-pressure boiler-room type sales practices." ALEC BALDWIN SUED BY ‘RUST’ PROP COMPANY OWNER ALLEGING ACTOR MADE HIM ‘SCAPEGOAT’ IN DEADLY ON-SET SHOOTING The Greenbergs claim they contacted Rosland in 2020 after seeing the television commercials promoting gold as a safe way to protect their wealth. Once put in touch with von Detten, one of the company's top advisors, the couple disclosed that their combined traditional IRA accounts contained more than $2 million. "Von Detten earned Sheila’s and Norman's trust. They believed him to be an expert and thus placed their faith completely in Von Detten to make the correct choices and recommendations and expressed as much to him," the court documents state. On Oct. 19, 2020, the Greenbergs allegedly followed von Detten’s recommendations and purchased more than $999,000 worth of Lady Liberty gold coins. The lawsuit claims Sheila paid $599,654.83 for 797 coins, while Norman paid $399,519.09 for 531 coins. "They believed that, however valued, Von Detten was taking care of them and the price they paid was a fair price for what they bought and the gold they purchased was worth the money they spent. Afterall, this was an IRA rollover. An investment intended to protect their hard-earned wealth for retirement." The complaint alleges the coins were sold at a premium of roughly 60%. The Greenbergs claim they paid the equivalent of $3,009.56 per ounce when the spot price of gold was approximately $1,903 per ounce. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? articles.title: The real history behind ‘Star Wars’: How real-world events inspired George Lucas’ iconic saga
articles.summary: Explore how real-world events, from Nazi Germany to the Vietnam War, influenced George Lucas's Star Wars. Discover the historical connections that made the iconic saga resonate with audiences across generations.
articles.body: In 1977, Star Wars lit up the big screen and carried audiences off to a galaxy of starships, glowing lightsabers and the oldest story of all, good against evil. But behind the science fiction was a story shaped by real events on Earth. George Lucas drew inspiration from wars, political leaders, ancient empires and historical warrior groups while creating his famous film series.Lucas himself acknowledged this connection in a 2005 interview with The Boston Globe. He said, “I love history, so while the psychological basis of ‘Star Wars’ is mythological, the political and social bases are historical.” His words offer a useful starting point for understanding the real-world ideas behind the saga.Nazi Germany and the Galactic EmpireThe Galactic Empire has several similarities to Nazi Germany, particularly in its uniforms, military displays and use of power. The Empire's stormtroopers are an obvious example. The name ‘Stormtroopers’ echoes the paramilitary forces tied to the Nazi Party, and the sharp, severe look of the Imperial officers brings to mind German military uniforms from World War II.Palpatine’s climb to power carries another historical echo. He starts as a politician, then uses fear and war to grab the Republic and turn it into an Empire, much like Hitler going from chancellor to dictator. That’s why the Empire feels so familiar, even in a galaxy far, far away. Lucas used recognisable historical imagery to make the struggle against authoritarian rule easier for audiences to understand.Richard Nixon and the rise of PalpatineOne of the more direct political influences behind Star Wars was former US president Richard Nixon. Lucas connected the original story to his concerns about American politics during the Vietnam War and Nixon's presidency. According to J.W. Rinzler's book The Making of Star Wars: Return of the Jedi, Lucas was asked in a 1981 story conference whether Palpatine had once been a Jedi. His answer was direct: “No, he was a politician. Richard M. Nixon was his name.”Lucas's interest was not limited to one politician. He was also concerned about how democratic governments could lose their power when leaders used public fear and political instability to gain more control.In a 2005 interview with the Chicago Tribune, he explained the idea behind the original film, saying, “the democracies aren’t overthrown; they’re given away.” The line captures one of the central themes of the saga.The Vietnam War and the Rebel AllianceThe Rebels versus the Empire is partly a nod to the Vietnam War, which was never far from Lucas’s mind while he was working on Star Wars.In the film, the Rebels are the underdogs. They’re smaller, with fewer weapons, fewer resources and far less military muscle than the Empire. But they refuse to back down and keep fighting an enemy that towers over them.This reflects a broader feature of the Vietnam conflict, where a smaller force used guerrilla tactics against a far more powerful military opponent. Lucas later connected the struggle of the Rebels to this imbalance of power.The influence can also be seen in Return of the Jedi. The Ewoks, despite their limited technology, help defeat Imperial forces by using their knowledge of the forest and their surroundings. Lucas discussed the Viet Cong's influence on the Ewoks in audio commentary for the film's 2004 re-release.Ancient Rome and the fall of the RepublicThe political structure of Star Wars also brings ancient Rome to mind. The Galactic Republic has a Senate, political representatives and a system of government that eventually gives way to an Empire.A similar transition took place in Roman history. Rome went from republic to empire slowly, with emperors gathering more and more power along the way. Star Wars does the same thing. Palpatine uses a time of war and chaos to turn the Republic into a dictatorship, one step at a timeThat comparison gives the story real depth. The Empire doesn’t appear overnight. Instead, the films show how a political system can change bit by bit, with its own institutions quietly paving the way.The Jedi and the Knights TemplarThe Jedi Order also has something in common with warrior groups from history. The Knights Templar were medieval religious knights, part monk and part soldier, who followed tough rules and took both their faith and their fighting seriously.The Jedi live by a code of their own. They practise discipline and are meant to use their gifts to protect peace. They aren’t the Templars in space, and their beliefs and structure are different, but the comparison shows how Lucas borrowed ideas from many corners of history to build his world.The Jedi also owe a lot to Japanese samurai traditions and martial arts films, which shaped how they look, how they carry themselves, and how they fight.Why the history behind ‘Star Wars’ still matters?Part of what keeps Star Wars alive all these years is how familiar its conflicts feel. Strip away the space battles and weird creatures, and what’s left are questions we all still argue about: who holds the power, when to fight back, who we stay loyal to, and what happens when fear runs the show.Lucas didn’t simply copy real events. He blended history with mythology and science fiction, which gave the saga a world all its own while keeping its struggles rooted in something human.The galaxy may be made up, but many of the ideas behind its wars and political fights trace back to Earth’s own past. That’s a big reason people keep coming back to Star Wars, long after the special effects have stopped being the main attraction and the characters have become old friends.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Jay Z's past political statements won't help perception of NFL politicizing Super Bowl halftime
articles.summary: Jay Z reportedly chose himself to perform the 2027 Super Bowl halftime show, but his extensive political history could deepen a troubling viewership trend.
articles.body: Bad Bunny's halftime performance this past February produced the largest drop in Super Bowl viewership during halftime in history. Specifically, viewership on NBC and Telemundo fell from 135.9 million at the end of the second quarter to 128.2 million during Bad Bunny's performance from 8:15 to 8:29 p.m. That's a 5.7% decline during halftime, compared to a 4% drop during Kendrick Lamar's performance a year earlier. Before the past two years, Super Bowl audiences had typically grown during the halftime show. According to Puck, the person responsible for selecting Lamar and Bad Bunny has now chosen himself to perform this year in Los Angeles: Jay Z, whom the NFL empowered as halftime czar in 2019. On the surface, a third consecutive year of declining halftime viewership should concern the league. Jay Z offers nostalgia. He was one of the defining hip-hop artists of the 2000s. He remained relevant well into the following decade through collaborations with artists such as Kanye West and Rihanna. More American viewers are likely to recognize Jay Z than Lamar or Bad Bunny, even if the latter is a massive international attraction. Still, recognition doesn't necessarily translate to interest. Lamar and Bad Bunny divided fans along political lines at a time when partisan activism often limits the appeal of an event as mainstream as the Super Bowl. Jay Z's political history is even more extensive. Sports fans may remember that he helped distribute "I Can’t Breathe" T-shirts as part of protests following the death of Eric Garner. He also headlined an Ohio concert for then-presidential candidate Hillary Clinton and was an outspoken supporter of Barack Obama. Jay Z celebrated Obama's election in the 2008 track "My President," rapping, "Rosa Parks sat so Martin Luther King could walk/Martin Luther King walked so Obama could run/Obama’s running so we all can fly." Is that so? Jay Z's political commentary has also included repeated criticism of Republicans, particularly President Donald Trump. He has called Trump "a joke," "not a very sophisticated man" and, during a 2018 CNN interview, a "superbug." He has also linked Trump's political rise to racism in America. "[Trump] cannot be my president. He cannot be our president," Jay Z said while campaigning for Clinton in 2016. He has also described America as "sexist" while discussing the country's failure to elect a female president. Anyway, Jay Z has now chosen to perform at the biggest annual entertainment event in this supposedly sexist and racist country. The NFL can argue that an artist's politics are irrelevant unless they surface during the halftime show. Maybe. But viewers don't necessarily make that distinction. Bad Bunny didn't make a political statement during his performance. He didn't have to. His anti-Trump commentary was already part of his public image, and a record share of the Super Bowl audience tuned out during his performance. The NFL understands this dynamic well. A poll last year found that it took nearly a decade for the league to regain its previous popularity among Republican-voting consumers after the national anthem protests began in 2016. The lesson should be obvious: alienating half the country is bad for business. The kneeling controversy hurt the NFL. The past two halftime shows have coincided with unusual audience declines. There is little reason to expect Jay Z to reverse that trend. Especially now that viewers have somewhere else to go. Turning Point USA's alternative halftime show was successful enough last season to establish an alternative for viewers who object to the NFL's selection on political grounds. The league can distance itself from Jay Z's selection by pointing to his authority over the halftime show. That's not convincing. No serious person believes Roger Goodell and the NFL are powerless to veto the performer at their own championship game. Of course they aren't. The NFL partnered with Jay Z's Roc Nation in 2019 to advise on live music entertainment and work with the league's Inspire Change initiative. The agreement came while the NFL was still navigating the political fallout from the Kaepernick controversy. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Seven years later, judge the arrangement by the results. The past two halftime shows lost viewers. And last season, many of them didn't return for the third quarter. While the uncompetitive Seahawks-Patriots matchup didn't help, overall Super Bowl viewership declined from 127.7 million in 2025 to 124.9 million in 2026. Considering Nielsen's change to its measurement system last year, the underlying decline is greater than the raw difference of nearly 3 million viewers suggests. We are not suggesting the NFL overcorrect by putting a conservative-leaning musician on stage. The Super Bowl doesn't need a Republican halftime show any more than it needs a Democratic one. It needs an artist with broad appeal who doesn't give millions of viewers another reason to change the channel. It should not be this difficult.
