articles.title: Matthew McConaughney urges voters to ditch two-party system
articles.summary: Matthew McConaughey is urging Americans to break up to the two-party system by voting independent in the November midterm elections.
articles.body:
Matthew McConaughey is making a case for Americans to break up the two-party system.

In a six-minute video posted to Instagram, McConaughey, 56, said electing independent candidates in the 2026 midterm elections and beyond could serve as a "permanent check" to keep Republicans and Democrats honest.

"And I am not here today to endorse a candidate, or a party," McConaughey said, adding that he was, however, endorsing two things: fairness and reality. "See, I believe in a fair fight and a fair fight is not just two fighters throwing the same punches at each other for 50 years. A fair fight is when the fighters who ought to be represented in the fight are actually in the fight."

The Oscar-winning actor urged voters to take independents more seriously, as they form part of the "No. 1 political identity in America today."

McConaughey also argued that independent candidates have the potential to wield significant power in a closely divided Congress, forcing both parties to "compete for the middle" rather than push legislation toward their respective extremes.

"The truth of it is, we don't know how many independents would vote for a true independent, organized, funded, owned by neither side, because no one has ever given us one," he said.

McConaughey referenced the Independent Leadership Council, launched by former Sen. Joe Manchin , and his daughter, to support independent congressional candidates. The "Interstellar" actor clarified he wasn't endorsing the organization, but rather the idea of giving voters another option.

"The reality is that midterms are coming, and this November, in more places than ever, you do have more than two choices," he said. "And I'm not telling you who to vote for. I'm telling you to look at your ballots, study up, see if they represent you, what you believe in."

While McConaughey's message was well received by some, others were critical of the timing, pointing out in the comment section that the stakes were too high to be "wasted" in the middle.

Matthew McConaughey hasn't ruled out running for office

A career in politics might still be in McConaughey's future. McConaughey , who has called himself " aggressively centrist " told People magazine last August that running for public office may have to wait until his three children are all grown up.

McConaughey shares Levi, 18, Vida, 16, and Livingston, 13, with his wife Camila Alves McConaughey, who he's been married to since 2012.

"For now, I'm very secure with — the original thing I knew I always wanted to be was a dad," McConaughey said, adding that he was still unsure by the prospect of a pivot but had started looking into it in 2019, and that it was a topic he continues to study.

"[Politics] is not necessarily my language, but that would happen if and when it was something that I couldn't not do," he said. "It would happen when I would look up and see that I'm pulled into it in a way that, 'Oh, I have to.'"

The "Brothers" star teased a potential campaign for the governor's seat in Texas back in 2021, but ultimately decided against getting in the race in the 2022 election cycle.

articles.title: Christina Applegate reveals she was 'misdiagnosed' with multiple sclerosis; says 'I haven’t gotten better... I’ve gotten worse'
articles.summary: Hollywood star Christina Applegate revealed some surprising news with all her fans as she returned to host her MeSsy podcast.
articles.body: Hollywood star Christina Applegate revealed some surprising news with all her fans as she returned to host her MeSsy podcast. The star, on Tuesday, surprised all when she revealed to co-host Jamie Lynn Sigler that she had been misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS).During her return to the podcast, Applegate shared that the reason she took time away from the podcast, was to process the news that she does not, in fact, have MS. Narrating the events of the day when she was informed that she was misdiagnosed, the actress shared, "She came into my room and said, ‘Congratulations, you don’t have MS'." Struggling to hold back her tears, she admitted, "I was, like, not happy at all. Everybody else was so happy."The actress also noted that despite learning that she didn't have the autoimmune disease, she claimed that it didn’t impact any of her debilitating symptoms.“You don’t get misdiagnosed and then all of the sudden I’m better,” Applegate said. She also admitted, “I haven’t gotten better, Jamie! If anything, I’ve gotten worse. So I’m back at square one where I don’t know what’s going on with me. And that’s going to be an online investigation that my doctors are going to be getting into just to find out what has been going on since 2021, why did this happen?”In the second part of the podcast, Applegate got emotional again, recalling the impact that the disease had on her personal and professional life. “I’ve gone through a great depression because of it. But I lost everything. I lost my job. I lost — I’m sorry. What do you say to someone who’s been living with this for six years — God, I’m so sorry — because it stopped my life. I still have to use wheelchairs when I go to the doctor’s office. I can’t walk from the car to the room. I’m still in this. Nothing magical happened when she said, ‘You don’t have MS.’ Nothing magical happened.”As per People, Dr. Marwa Kaisey, associate professor with the Cedars-Sinai Medical Centre Department of Neurology, who joined Applegate and Sigler for the second episode of the podcast, said, MS misdiagnoses are “fairly common” due to the fact that “we don’t have one single test for MS. The Kerala Story, The Kashmir Files, and The Bengal Files - all of these will be (or have been) made tax-free, and the same will apply to Ramayana," he said.Adhikari also spoke about the growing slate of films based on Indian mythology, and even expressed his excitement fror the epic Mahabharata. He said, "In the days to come, we will see films on Shri Krishna and Arjuna, as well as the Mahabharata."This announcement came shortly after Producer Namit Malhotra announced a multi-project Ramayana Cinematic Universe. articles.title: Prince Harry says ‘most important thing is to reconcile’ with royal family
articles.summary: Prince Harry says reconciliation with King Charles III and Prince William is key, but a spokesperson clarified his remark about those who "don't want to work it out."
articles.body: Prince Harry is ready to put the past behind him as he makes a renewed plea for reconciliation with the royal family. During a video interview with GQ that was conducted by the magazine's host Zach Baron in September and released Tuesday, the 42-year-old Duke of Sussex was asked whether he grieved his complicated relationships with his father King Charles III, 77, and his brother Prince William, 44. "Yes, of course," Harry said. "I think from a family perspective — again, another massively relatable issue for so many people — sibling disagreements, broken relationships between kids and their parents, kids and one parent. That continues to come up with me the whole time with people that I speak to, so I know how relatable it is." PRINCE HARRY RISKS 'LOBBING A GRENADE' AT PRINCE WILLIAM AS CHANCE TO HEAL YEARS-LONG FEUD EMERGES: EXPERT "Some people maybe look at us and go, ‘How are you gonna work it out? Maybe that will help me work my stuff out,'" he continued. "Some people don't want it to work out," Harry added. "I want it to work out. With everything else that's going on in the world, the most important thing is to reconcile — that's the key point." PRINCE WILLIAM'S ABSENCE SPEAKS VOLUMES AS KING CHARLES REUNITES WITH PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE: EXPERTS Baron went on to ask Harry if he believes the family "wound" can be repaired to which Harry replied, "Scars stick around forever." "But what your perception is, and what your mindset is to those things that have happened, letting go of the past," he said. "That's something that I would encourage everybody to do: If there's certain things from the past that are still affecting you every day, that's harder to let go of." "But, for me, there's enough drama in the world and enough drama in people's lives to continue with issues with family," Harry added. Following the interview's release, Harry's comment that "some people don't want it to work out" sparked speculation that he was referring to William. A spokesperson later clarified Harry's remark, telling People magazine that his comment "was absolutely not intended as a swipe at his brother or any other member of his family." PRINCE WILLIAM ‘INCANDESCENT WITH ANGER’ AT PRINCE HARRY AS DIANA ANNIVERSARY DEEPENS ROYAL RIFT: PIERS MORGAN "The comment was made in a general context and was not directed at his family in any way," Harry's representative added. Harry's relationship with his family has been strained for years. Rumors of a rift between the brothers began to swirl in 2018 after Harry married former "Suits" star Meghan Markle. Harry publicly acknowledged problems in his relationship with William in October 2019, telling ITV that although they would "always be brothers," they were on "different paths" and don't see each other as often as they did in the past. PRINCE WILLIAM AND KATE MIDDLETON 'PLAYING IT COOL' AS PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE RETURN TO THE UK: EXPERT Tensions escalated further after Harry and Markle stepped back as senior working royals in January 2020 and relocated to Canada before settling in California. The Duke and Duchess of Sussex later aired grievances against the royal family in their bombshell 2021 interview with Oprah Winfrey. During the television special, Harry and Markle alleged a lack of support from the institution and accused an unnamed royal family member of racism. Harry also opened up about his strained relationships with Charles and William, though he shared his hopes that those could be repaired. He admitted that he felt "really let down" by Charles and revealed that his father had stopped taking his calls as the Sussexes prepared to step down from their royal roles. PRINCE HARRY'S SECURITY FIGHT THREATENS HIGHLY-ANTICIPATED REUNION WITH KING CHARLES: EXPERT However, Harry said he would "always love" his father and vowed to "make it one of my priorities to try and heal that relationship." Harry addressed his rift with William, saying he loved his brother "to bits" but said again that they were on "different paths." At the time, he described their relationship as "space" while expressing hope that "time heals all things." PRINCE WILLIAM ‘BLINDSIDED’ BY HARRY, MEGHAN RETURN AS KATE FEARS NEW TURMOIL FROM ROYAL FEUD: EXPERTS A year later, the couple's relationship with the royal family deteriorated further with the release of their Netflix series "Harry & Meghan." In the series, Harry accused the royal institution of leaking and planting stories and further detailed the breakdown in his relationship with his family. The rift deepened following the January 2023 publication of Harry's memoir, "Spare," in which he detailed private disputes with his father and brother and alleged that William physically attacked him during a 2019 argument over Markle. Buckingham Palace declined to respond publicly to Harry's allegations. PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE’S UK MOVE PUTS FRESH SPOTLIGHT ON THEIR EXPLOSIVE CLAIMS AGAINST ROYAL FAMILY However, Harry has continued to express his desire to reconcile with his family. In a January 2023 interview with ITV while promoting "Spare," Harry said, "Forgiveness is 100% a possibility because I would like to get my father back. I would like to have my brother back." "At the moment, I don't recognize them, as much as they probably don't recognize me," he added. At the time, Harry said that reconciliation would only be possible under one condition. "Though I would like to have reconciliation, I would like accountability," he said. "I've managed to make peace over this time with a lot of things that have happened. But that doesn't mean that I'm just gonna let it go." Harry's latest remarks echo comments he made last year when he publicly called for an end to his long-running feud with the royal family. During an interview with the BBC in May 2025, Harry's rhetoric shifted noticeably after losing his legal challenge over his security in the United Kingdom. "I would love reconciliation with my family," he said. "There’s no point in continuing to fight any more. Life is precious." "I don’t know how much longer my father has," Harry added. In February 2024, Charles was diagnosed with an unspecified form of cancer, and he continues receiving ongoing medical treatment. The Duke of Sussex also indicated that he had forgiven his family for many of their past disagreements. articles.title: Heath Ledger and James Avery honored by former co-stars on ‘Dancing with the Stars’
articles.summary: Actors Julia Stiles and Tatyana Ali dedicated their Week 6 dances to the two men, sharing emotional tributes with fans through their choreography.
articles.body: There was not a dry eye in the ballroom Tuesday night after celebrities competing on “Dancing with the Stars” paid tribute to those who left an impact on them, who included actors Heath Ledger and James Avery. The dedication week is a tradition for the reality series, often leading to emotional moments on the normally lighthearted dance series. Among those competing this season are actors Julia Stiles and Tatyana Ali, who chose to honor their former co-stars. Stiles reflected on her time with Ledger while they were filming their ’90s rom-com “10 Things I Hate About You,” in which Ledger’s role as the mischievous Patrick Verona solidified him as a teen heartthrob. Ledger died in 2008 of an accidental overdose caused by mixing painkillers and sedatives that were prescribed to him. In her rehearsal package, Stiles recalled how authentic Ledger was during the filming. She teared up talking about how easy it was working with him. She and her partner, Ezra Sosa, did a contemporary dance to a cover of Frankie Valli’s “Can’t Take My Eyes Off of You.” It was an homage to a famous scene from the movie in which Ledger’s character serenades Stiles. “I have so many great memories, but I’m also sad, because I really wish that I could pick up the phone and be like: ‘Hey, dude, people really care about that movie. We did something special,’” Stiles said. “And I can’t do that.” Before the episode aired, the partners posted a joint Instagram statement saying the dance was about honoring “a film that changed so many lives, and someone whose impact continues to be felt by generations.” Stiles ended her dance by placing a rose down in front of a photo of Ledger. When she turned back, the entire main cast of “10 Things I Hate About You” was on the dance floor to join her. Actors Andrew Keegan, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Larisa Oleynik, Susan May Pratt and Gabrielle Union joined hands with Stiles as the music faded. Judge Derek Hough thanked the cast for joining Stiles for the moment after the performance ended. “I mean, how cool is it to have created something that will last forever, you know?” Hough said. “And tonight, this performance will last forever, as well. It was a perfect combination of joy, fun and emotion.” Stiles earned a combined total of 36 from the four judges, her best score of the competition series so far. Another poignant dedication came from the former cast members of the “Fresh Prince of Bel-Air,” as Ali and Alfonso Ribeiro danced in honor of Avery, their on-screen father. Avery, who portrayed Uncle Phil on the series, died on New Year’s Eve in 2013 following complications from open-heart surgery. Before the episode, Ali posted a TikTok video explaining how much Avery meant to her. She spoke about how he offered her mentorship and “poured” into her at a young age. “I met him when I was 11 years old,” Ali said. “Every holiday, James would give me a baby doll. I have a collection of beautiful baby dolls. And he told me, ‘I’m giving you these dolls because they look like you, and I always want you to know how beautiful you are.’” In the segment showing her rehearsals, Ali said she “loved him a lot.” Ribeiro called it a blessing of his life to be able to do the dance with Ali. Ribeiro, Ali and her partner, Jan Ravnik, danced a Viennese waltz to Nancy Wilson’s “(You Don’t Know) How Glad I Am.” The song was a cover recorded by Ali, who said Wilson was one of Avery’s favorite artists. During the dance, Ravnik left Ali on the dance floor and allowed Ribeiro to end the performance with her. The two shared a tearful hug when the music stopped, with a portrait of Avery on display behind them. The four judges gave Ali a combined score of 32, her best of the season. Judge Carrie Ann Inaba said she felt honored to be able to watch the former on-screen siblings dance together. “Dance plays a role in our lives, like, a real role,” Inaba said. “And tonight, I saw it play this role right here live. And you dance like — it was like watching an old Hollywood film come to life, and all of your grace.”

articles.title: Vijay Sethupathi's Chennai house: Look into 'Baththa' actor's reported Rs 50 Cr property and other investments
articles.summary: Vijay Sethupathi is surely one of the most versatile actors in Tamil cinema.
articles.body: Vijay Sethupathi is surely one of the most versatile actors in Tamil cinema. Known as Makkal Selvan, meaning People's Treasure, the actor has appeared in Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam and Hindi films. Born Vijaya Gurunatha Sethupathi Kalimuthu on January 16, 1978, he worked several jobs before establishing himself as an actor. His latest film, 'Baththa', is a 2026 Tamil comedy-drama directed by Balaji Tharaneetharan.Vijay Sethupathi's Chennai house and estimated valueVijay Sethupathi reportedly owns a residence in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, where he lives away from the constant attention surrounding his professional life. Eazemyrent website reports have placed the property's estimated value at around Rs 50 crore. However, this figure has not been independently verified, and the exact address has not been publicly confirmed.Property investments in ChennaiApart from his reported primary residence, Vijay Sethupathi has been linked to properties in several Chennai neighbourhoods. These reportedly include a residential property in Kilpauk, land associated with Ennore in North Chennai, and an office in Valasaravakkam used for his production activities.The actor has maintained a relatively private approach to his finances. Publicly available information does not establish the precise ownership details or current market values of these properties. Early life and education in North ChennaiAccording to the actor's official website, Vijay Sethupathi was born in Rajapalayam on January 16, 1978. He studied at MGR Higher Secondary School and Little Angels Matriculation Higher Secondary School. The actor has described himself as an average student during his school days.At the age of 16, he auditioned for 'Nammavar' but did not secure a role because of his height, as reported by Bhaskar English. Rather than entering films immediately, he took up various jobs and eventually completed a Bachelor of Commerce degree at Jain College. He later worked as an accounts assistant.From a Dubai job to an acting careerSeeking better financial opportunities, Vijay Sethupathi moved to Dubai in the United Arab Emirates, where he worked in a corporate position. During his stay, he met Jessie. The two dated for two years before getting married.Despite earning more than he had in India, Vijay eventually returned home because he was dissatisfied with his job. He subsequently joined a marketing company dealing in ready-made kitchens. His interest in acting resurfaced after he came across a theatre poster associated with Koothu-P-Pattarai. An earlier observation by filmmaker Balu Mahendra about his photogenic face also encouraged him to pursue cinema seriously.Career breakthrough and latest filmVijay Sethupathi began working in films in 2006, initially appearing in background roles and smaller parts. His breakthrough arrived with 'Thenmerku Paruvakaatru' (2010), directed by Seenu Ramasamy, in which he played the lead character.The year 2012 proved particularly important, with 'Pizza', 'Naduvula Konjam Pakkatha Kaanom' and 'Sundarapandian' showcasing his range. He subsequently took on leading roles, antagonists and unconventional characters across multiple film industries.Outside his career, Vijay Sethupathi has also explored family-oriented storytelling through 'Mughizh', a film featuring relationships between family members and a pet dog. His latest release, 'Baththa', reunites him with Tamil cinema audiences in an emotional drama directed by Balaji Tharaneetharan. articles.title: 'Success still unreal' says Gruffalo artist before Hastings Storytelling Festival
articles.summary: Axel Scheffler's illustrations helped turn The Gruffalo series into a global literary phenomenon.
articles.body:
The illustrator who created The Gruffalo and helped spawn a global literary phenomenon has said the series' popularity still "doesn't seems real".

Axel Scheffler, who drew the pictures for the best-selling books, first collaborated with their author Julia Donaldson, from Steyning in West Sussex, in the early '90s.

This weekend he will be appearing at the annual Hastings Storytelling Festival, of which he is patron, where he'll be reading, sketching and signing copies of some of his best known titles.

"To have had such huge success, especially worldwide, just seems completely unbelievable to me," he said.

With The Gruffalo thought to have reached up to 18.2m sales worldwide since its release in 1999, Scheffler explained how he first came up with look of its now iconic eponymous creature.

"I started sketching and thought, 'Gruffalo? That sounds like buffalo' - so I gave him some horns, a tail and some fur," said the 68-year-old West German.

"I also knew he needed to be threatening, but not too scary.

"Actually, when they saw my first draft the publishers asked me to make him a little less frightening," added Scheffler, who went through "10 to 15" versions of The Gruffalo before settling on the finished version.

"But whenever I do school visits and ask the children about this, they always go for the more scary ones. So publishers aren't always right."

With two sequels under his belt since then - including 2004's The Gruffalo's Child and this year's Gruffalo Granny - Scheffler considers books to be "more important than ever" these days.

"The statistics suggest fewer parents are reading to their children, who, in turn, are spending more time looking at screens," he said.

"That's why picture books are good at creating a link between adults and children when it comes to reading together.

"I like that they have images which don't move, because it really gets kids to focus on all the little details."

Scheffler added he is looking forward to appearing at Hasting's White Rock Theatre this Saturday.

"I get a lot of affection and admiration from the children at these sorts of events," he said.

"But it's the parents who are usually more excited to meet me."

articles.title: Vidya Balan still hungry for role like ‘The Dirty Picture’: ‘I am greedy actor’
articles.summary: Vidya Balan hasn’t lost her appetite for a role like 'The Dirty Picture', the 2011 film that changed the course of her career 15 years ago.
articles.body: Vidya Balan hasn’t lost her appetite for a role like 'The Dirty Picture', the 2011 film that changed the course of her career 15 years ago. Her stint as Silk Smitha won her the National Film Award for Best Actress, and the actor says she would be glad to tackle another challenging character of that kind.Vidya Balan open to another challenging role like Silk SmithaEktaa Kapoor has announced 'The Dirty Picture 2', and Balan is excited about the franchise coming back, even though she feels Silk’s story has already been told. Speaking to Variety India, she said: “The hunger and the craving are still very much there. Whatever the role, I’m just a greedy actor. I’ve said this a million times before, and I’ll say it a billion times more: If a project inspires me, I will dive right into it headlong without a second thought.”Vidya Balan on ‘The Dirty Picture 2’'The Dirty Picture 2' is officially in the works, Ektaa has confirmed, 15 years after the original was released. Nothing has been revealed yet about who will star in the sequel or whom it will center on, but the producer has said she has found a story she wants to bring to the screen. Balan, though, is firm that a return to the franchise would only make sense if the story moved past the life of the character she played the first time.“Of course, I know Silk cannot take part, so I really don't know. I heard from my manager that there is news about Ekta announcing 'The Dirty Picture 2', and I'm thrilled about it. The Dirty Picture gives you so much scope for a different story each time. So let's see what happens. If she approaches me, I will definitely be thrilled, but honestly, Silk's story is over. So it would have to be something like that to explore again,” Balan said.‘The Dirty Picture’ released in 2011'The Dirty Picture' was released in 2011 and also featured Naseeruddin Shah, Emraan Hashmi and Tusshar Kapoor in key roles. articles.title: McLaren held fresh talks after Singapore GP clash as Lando Norris promises to "make better decisions"
articles.summary: McLaren has held further talks on Lando Norris' Singapore Grand Prix sprint race clash with Oscar Piastri as the team now considers the matter case closed
articles.body:
Lando Norris has conceded he needs to make "better decisions" as McLaren aims to draw a line under his clash with team-mate Oscar Piastri in Singapore.

Norris drew the ire of his team management for taking out both himself and Piastri with a lunge for fourth place in the Singapore sprint race, costing the team valuable points in the championship and going against its racing principles.

Team principal Andrea Stella said after the Singapore race that the team would hold further talks at its Woking factory to avoid a repeat. It is understood those talks happened last week, and that the team is now keen to move on from the incident as Norris apologised for his error of judgement.

"I take responsibility for my mistakes, and I learn from them," Norris was quoted in the team's United States Grand Prix preview. "This team is my motivation every weekend, and my aim is to repay the hard work everyone puts in by improving, making better decisions, and representing the team in the best possible way."

Norris's clash with his team-mate added to what had been a tough triple-header as McLaren had no answer for the significant performance upgrades Red Bull was able to add to its car, leading to back-to-back wins for Max Verstappen in Malaysia and Singapore.

"After a difficult triple-header, we take the lessons learned from both our performance and execution and put them into action," Stella added. "In F1, success is never guaranteed – so our response is to keep building, keep developing, and keep pushing forward together as one team."

Lando Norris, McLaren, Oscar Piastri, McLaren

McLaren brings latest round of upgrades after performance falls flat

McLaren had brought its own upgrades to the MCL40 too, and while it was left confused by its lack of performance in Malaysia, Singapore further underlined that while its own upgrades appear to work as intended, it had simply been out-developed by Red Bull, while Ferrari was also extremely strong on the high-downforce Singapore street circuit and Mercedes has also added performance to its car.

McLaren is now bringing its latest round of relatively minor upgrades to the car at this weekend's race in Austin, largely focused on the front of the car, as it hopes the Circuit of the Americas will suit the car better than the likes of Baku and Singapore did. It has also applied further tweaks to make its drivers feel more confident under braking.

"We're bringing a modest selection of upgrades for this event, aimed at improving some braking reliability and performance issues," said chief designer Rob Marshall. "We also have some small floor changes to test.

"We have all seen how difficult it is to predict the relative performance of the top teams over the last five or six races. Obviously, there are many factors in play here: cars being upgraded, cars suiting and drivers liking certain circuits among other factors. The last few races have not been great for us, but I think we're getting stronger again and Austin is probably a better circuit for our car."
